rationale: Round 4, lens: AC falsifiability and internal consistency, re-read from disk at a593792a. All 4 of my round-3 asks are ADDRESSED: the follow-up-bug shape is now class N4 under a plan-mapped membership (R1.1 (c), R1.2, AC-1 row O, AC-4 (v) rewritten, the lifecycle-first default pick rejected with its reason); AC-1's fake is edge-only and G' carries the numeric-only tag, with Background A and the Validation Proof now admitting that the full-ID reporter shape is green today on bd 1.1.0; an indeterminate record refuses the scoped override before mutation (R6.1, AC-15, touchpoint (iii)); AC-11 (vii) now pins that reattest REFUSES with UnlandedReview and writes nothing. The finder-only redesign is internally consistent on the text: FindLandedMergeReachable returns a typed off-first-parent result that wraps ErrLandedMergeNotFound and not NoCandidate, R4.4 gains arm 1b ahead of arm 2, the read-back is grounded on reattest's existing mindspec_landed_reattest_scanned_branch audit key (verified in internal/lifecycle/reattest.go), the per-record digests make VALID/coverage/AC-16/AC-17 agree, and mindspec-wtjr exists live. One MAJOR remains, and it is the scoping the BRIEF invited us to attack: R4.2's reattest refusal (ii) (any registered reviewed_head_sha not an ancestor of the tip) is justified on the primary path by 'a rebased-away review round is normal (ADR-0041 §2(i))', but that same normal shape on a bead that later sits off the first-parent chain makes the fallback candidate unacceptable by reattest, so Goal (d)'s and Provenance's claim that #239 is 'recoverable by one audited command' is false for it, no residual is stated, and no AC covers it. Minors: R1.1 (c)'s fail-closed plan.md read conflicts with AC-4 (iv) for a plan-phase spec (readiness reads <specDir>/plan.md from the invoking checkout, which does not exist before plan approve); AC-1's red-on-revert claims for O and X need their titles pinned to contain S; R1.3's N4-positional exception has no AC leg; AC-11 (x) cites a reviewer's scratch probe file instead of describing the topology; R6.5's new staged line has no removal date although ADR-0045 Decision 5 requires one for new staged content.
concrete_changes_required: R4.2 refusal (ii) / Goal (d) / Provenance / AC-11: the fallback-only UnlandedReview refusal fires on the shape the spec itself calls normal — a review round whose reviewed_head_sha was rebased away (ADR-0041 §2(i)) — whenever that bead's landing later sits off the first-parent chain, so '#239 is recoverable by one audited command' is false there. Do one of: (a) state the residual in R4.2 and Goal (d), name the only remaining exit (the ADR-0035 mindspec-q9ea attested-restore marker, Spec-125 datum (e)), and add an AC-11 leg: #239 topology with registrations {A rebased away, B = second parent} → MF-3 FAILS naming the candidate and reattest REFUSES UnlandedReview naming A, writes nothing; or (b) refine (ii) so it refuses only when a non-ancestor registration is a LATER round than every registration that equals the candidate's second parent (O3's shape: later reviewed work never landed), accepts the earlier-round rebased-away case, and pin both legs in AC-11 (the (vii)/(viii) shapes still refuse; the rebased-away-earlier-round shape is accepted with the audit recording the non-ancestor SHA).

R1.1 (c) vs AC-4 (iv): readiness reads plan.md via os.ReadFile(<specDir>/plan.md) in the invoking checkout (internal/validate/readiness/readiness.go), which does not exist for an approved-but-unplanned spec, and R1.1 says an unreadable plan.md 'refuses the whole command fail-closed'. That contradicts AC-4 (iv) (stored plan, zero lifecycle children → `recovery: mindspec plan approve S`) and would make every scoped `next` on a plan-phase spec refuse. Make the plan.md read lazy — only when at least one plan-form row with lineage E needs mapping — and pin AC-4 (iv) with no plan.md on disk; state which checkout's specDir is read.

AC-1 red-on-revert: 'O is selected and then refused by MF-1' and 'X is selected and then fails readiness on lineage E2' hold today only if O's and X's titles pass containsSpecID. Pin both titles as containing the full spec ID (the follow-up convention), or drop those two red-on-revert claims.

AC-3: add the N4-positional leg that R1.3 introduces — `mindspec next <E>.7 --spec S` (unmapped follow-up) reaches GateReadiness and refuses NOT-READY on MF-1 with the scoped recovery line; `--allow-not-ready=MF-1 --evidence <f>` then claims it and records `signals: [MF-1]`. Today the positional is refused as 'not in the ready set' only if the title filter dropped it, so state the red-on-revert leg precisely.

AC-11 (x): describe the two-candidate topology in the AC itself (which two admitted short-form merges, their second parents, and the empty sibling merge that anchored the revert mask) instead of citing `repo/internal/lifecycle/g3_round3_probe_test.go`, a reviewer's scratch file that will not exist when the bead is implemented.

R6.5 / ADR-0045 Decision 5: the remaining `ms-bead-impl` line is NEW staged content, and Decision 5 requires a target AND a removal date at staging; the transition clause grandfathers pre-existing skill content only. Either give the line a provisional removal condition now (e.g. 'removed when `next-action` ships, spec 133; date set no later than the spec-130 rule table') and say so in the skill text, or extend the transition clause explicitly to rules staged by specs 129–133 before step 1 lands, and reflect that in AC-18.

findings.title: Round-3 ask status
findings.detail: F2r3.1 (plan-form follow-up bug is a member) ADDRESSED via Ruling 2 — R1.1 (c) requires MF-1's own plan mapping; bd's minting of `<E>.<N>` for any child is stated with live examples (mindspec-cter.8, mindspec-jfgj.4); unmapped children are class N4, informational, never default-picked; AC-1 row O and AC-4 (v) rewritten; my lifecycle-first default-pick alternative is rejected with a stated reason (MF-1 would refuse the member anyway), which I accept. F2r3.2 (AC-1 bead G red-on-revert) ADDRESSED — the fake bd's `--parent` is edge-only, G' carries the numeric-only tag, Background A and the Validation Proof state that the full-ID shape is selected today on bd 1.1.0. F2r3.3 (indeterminate record under a scoped override) ADDRESSED — R6.1 'Indeterminate failures' bullet refuses before mutation; AC-15 leg; ADR-0041 touchpoint (iii). F2r3.4 (AC-11 vii write outcome) ADDRESSED — reattest REFUSES with ReattestStateUnlandedReview naming B and writes nothing; (viii)/(ix) extend it. Totals: 4 ADDRESSED, 0 PARTIAL, 0 MISSED; 1 NEW_ISSUE (the rebased-away-round scoping) raised below as invited by the BRIEF.

findings.title: The fallback-only UnlandedReview refusal makes #239 unrecoverable for the review shape the spec calls normal
findings.detail: R4.2 (ii): reattest on a fallback candidate 'refuses with ReattestStateUnlandedReview' if ANY registered reviewed_head_sha is not an ancestor of the spec tip, and the rule is scoped to fallback candidates because 'on the primary path a rebased-away review round is normal, and refusing there would create an ADR-0041 §2(i) deadlock'. The same normal event — round-1 reviewed at A, the branch rebased, round-2 reviewed and landed at B, registrations {A, B} — is indistinguishable, by the (ii) test, from O3's attack shape (B reviewed later and never landed). When such a bead's landing later sits off the first-parent chain (the #239 topology is a property of the spec branch's later history, not of the bead), the automatic path names the candidate (correct), reattest refuses on A (by rule), and nothing in the spec accepts it: Goal (d) and the Provenance paragraph say #239 is 'recoverable by one audited command', R4.2 lists no residual for this case, and AC-11 has no leg for it ((vii)–(ix) all have the unlanded SHA as the LATER round). Either the primary-path normality claim is true, in which case the fallback has the same exposure and the spec must say what the exit is, or it is not, in which case the scoping rationale fails. The round ordering is available (panel registrations carry `round`), so a refinement that refuses only when the non-ancestor SHA belongs to a later round than any registration equal to the second parent would separate the two shapes.

findings.title: R1.1 (c)'s fail-closed plan.md read contradicts AC-4 (iv) for a plan-phase spec
findings.detail: readiness.go line ~139 reads plan.md with os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(specDir, "plan.md")) in the invoking checkout. Before plan approve there is no plan.md, and R1.1 says 'an unreadable plan.md refuses the whole command fail-closed (`could not read plan.md for <S>`)' and that it is 'read once per scoped call'. AC-4 (iv) expects `recovery: mindspec plan approve S` for exactly that spec state. The read must be lazy (only when a plan-form row with lineage E needs mapping) or a missing plan.md must be 'maps nothing' when the epic has no children; AC-4 (iv) should pin the no-plan.md fixture.

findings.title: AC-1's red-on-revert claims for O and X depend on unpinned titles
findings.detail: Today's selection applies containsSpecID after `bd ready --parent`; O (`<E>.7`, parent E, bug) and X (`<E>.8`, parent E) are 'selected today' only if their titles contain the full spec ID. The fixture lists no title for either.

findings.title: R1.3's N4-positional exception has no AC
findings.detail: R1.3: 'an N4 positional is passed to GateReadiness, which refuses it NOT-READY on MF-1. A scoped, evidenced --allow-not-ready=MF-1 can then claim it deliberately.' AC-2 pins only that no `bd update` recovery is offered and AC-3 has no N4 leg, so the one route the spec offers for follow-up children is unpinned.

findings.title: AC-11 (x) is defined by reference to a reviewer's scratch probe
findings.detail: 'This is the fixture from G3's repo/internal/lifecycle/g3_round3_probe_test.go' — a file under a panel slot's scratch directory, not in the repository. The AC needs the topology in its own words to be runnable by the implementing bead.

findings.title: R6.5's staged line has no removal date while ADR-0045 Decision 5 requires one
findings.detail: ADR-0045 Decision 5: a rule staged in a skill 'must show the ID of its target gate or config key, and a removal date'. R6.5 names the target (next-action, spec 133) and defers the date to the spec-130 rule table. The round-3 transition clause (as summarised in Impacted Domains and AC-18) grandfathers PRE-EXISTING skill content until step 7; the `ms-bead-impl` ready-check line is new content written by this spec.

findings.title: Verified against a593792a / live tools (no change needed)
findings.detail: Reattest already writes mindspec_landed_reattest_{actor,at,op,corroboration,prior_merge_sha,prior_second_parent,scanned_branch} (internal/lifecycle/reattest.go), so R4.2's read-back condition ('a reattest audit record whose scanned branch is this spec branch') is grounded; ReattestStateNoOwnedMerge/Ambiguous/TipContradiction/PanelContradiction exist and UnlandedReview is new as stated. Forgery attack on the read-back: a forged binding plus forged audit keys passes the fallback read, which is the same class as a forged binding passing datum (d) on the primary path today; the spec states this residual and ADR-0037 §8 accepts it, so the fallback read-back is not weaker than the primary path. FindEpicForBeadWithCache resolves the first epic-typed dependency before the title fallback, so N2b's `bd update --parent` repair and N2c's classification are consistent with the code; its title fallback is fmt.Sscanf("%d"), so G' resolves. bd mints `<E>.<N>` for bug and feature children (my round-3 probe), matching R1.1's new paragraph. R4.4 arm 1b precedes arm 2 and the typed result wraps ErrLandedMergeNotFound but not NoCandidate, so the discrimination is well-ordered. R6.2 per-record digests, R6.3 VALID (non-empty sorted duplicate-free list per signal), R6.4 subset coverage, AC-16's growth/shrink/multiplicity legs and AC-17's mixed-coverage legs are mutually consistent; the re-claim line names all failing signals, consistent with replace-never-union. AC-4 (v) is now the reparented/non-plan-form and N4 shapes, exit 0, consistent with R1.2. mindspec-wtjr exists in the live database (P2 bug, 2026-10-18). Background K's Atoi/Sscanf mechanism matches internal/approve/spec.go parseSpecID and the derive.go fallback.
